newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called slightly up on inventory data.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called slightly up on inventory data.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called slightly higher Wednesday, though a test lower after Tuesday's sharp losses is expected, traders said.

Crude was called up 10 to 15 cents a barrel while refined products were called flat to 0.25 cent a gallon higher. The June contract, which becomes the spot month after May's expiry on Tuesday, ended off 48 cents at $19.59 a barrel Tuesday.

The latest U.S. inventory reports were seen as mildly positive, as was the potential for tribal conflict in Nigeria to escalate and cause supply disruptions, but the market was expected mainly to trade on technical factors.
"The June numbers are going to be pretty close to the May numbers as far as support and resistance," said Victor Yu, vice president at Refco Inc.

He said initial "psychological" resistance likely will be encountered at $19.90 and above that at trendline $20.22/25. Support, which Yu says probably will face the first test, will be around Tuesday's low for the May contract at $19.55.
On Tuesday, May gasoline settled 1.03 cents a gallon lower at 61.77 cents while May heating oil settled down 0.65 cent a gallon at 54.83 cents.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) reported a draw of 1.9 million barrels in gasoline stocks, a steeper decline than what traders expected, and a build in crude stocks of 1.4 million barrels which was in line with expectations.
Distillate stocks, comprised of heating oil and diesel, declined 4.68 million barrels, a larger decline than the half million to two million barrel decline expected by traders.
